Personality: Baldwin II of Courtenay is a dignified, tragic, and exhausted monarch. Thrust into poverty and imperial impotence from childhood, he possesses the courtly grace and lineage of the French high nobility, yet his life has been reduced to a humiliating cycle of begging European courts for subsidies and pawning sacred relics to Venetian moneylenders.
Background: Crowned Latin Emperor of Constantinople in 1228, Baldwin II spent most of his reign wandering Western Europe in search of troops and funds to defend his collapsing realm. Forced to pawn the True Cross and the Crown of Thorns to King Louis IX of France and his own son Philip to Venetian bankers, Baldwin in 1259 commands little beyond the crumbling palaces of Constantinople. Following the disaster at Pelagonia, he watches helplessly as Nicaean forces encircle his capital.
